issues.description: Guard fires for every non-Tab key, breaking arrow/Escape/Backspace navigation of the popup
issues.detail: The condition `not get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` triggers for Up/Down/PageUp/PageDown/Escape/Backspace and printable chars, not just Enter. When the setting is off, the popup hides and forwards on first arrow press, making navigation unusable. Scope the check to Key_Return/Key_Enter explicitly.

issues.description: Double-negative condition `not ... and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` obscures the intended predicate
issues.detail: The reader must mentally invert twice to recover intent. Use `key != Qt.Key_Tab`, parenthesize, and ideally name the predicate (e.g. `enter_accept_disabled`). The logic isn't wrong but the shape hides the rule it encodes and the name `use_enter_for_completions` doesn't match a `not Tab` test.

issues.description: Re-dispatching the QKeyEvent to textedit.keyPressEvent after hide() is a layering hack
issues.detail: Forwarding the event from inside the popup's handler risks double-handling, focus issues, and recursion if the editor re-shows the popup. The correct shape is to call event.ignore() (or simply not consume it) and let Qt's normal event propagation deliver it to the editor.

issues.description: get_conf() called on every keystroke instead of cached on the widget
issues.detail: The config lookup runs per key event while the popup is visible. Read the setting once at popup show-time (or cache it and invalidate via a config-change signal). This separates policy-as-value from event handling and removes per-keystroke lookup latency in a hot path.

issues.description: No test exercises the False branch of the new toggle
issues.detail: `use_enter_for_completions` defaults True in the schema, preserving behavior, but there is no test for the False path. For a user-facing behavior toggle in completion handling, at least one regression test covering Enter-not-accepting (and popup navigation still working) is cheap insurance.

issues.description: New branch lacks a comment explaining intent and precedes the `item is None` guard
issues.detail: The new early-return block has no comment stating why Enter should be forwarded when the setting is off, and it intentionally runs before the `item is None` fallback. One literate sentence above the `if` would let a cold reader reconstruct the intent without grepping the config key.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, well-intentioned patch with the wrong shape in the key-handling branch. The condition `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` overreaches: it fires for arrow keys, Escape, Backspace and printable characters, which will make the popup unusable when the toggle is off. The double-negative reads poorly and should be a named predicate scoped specifically to Return/Enter. Secondary issues: re-dispatching the event into textedit is a layering hack better replaced by event.ignore(), get_conf() should be cached rather than read per keystroke, and at least one test should cover the False branch. NEEDS-WORK before landing.
